title: Why Mark Rossini’s Name Remains Central to the Puerto Rico Corruption Debate
shortdescription: Mark Rossini’s federal case has ended, but his name remains central to Puerto Rico’s continuing debate over political influence, campaign money, and presidential clemency. The reason is not only the pardon itself.

description.subtitle: From Former FBI Agent to Central Figure in a Puerto Rico Political Corruption Case
description.text: Mark Rossini's name became widely associated with Puerto Rico's public corruption debate following the federal investigation involving former governor Wanda Vázquez Garced and international banker Julio Herrera Velutini. A former FBI supervisory special agent, Rossini was accused by federal prosecutors of acting as an intermediary in an alleged arrangement involving campaign financing and influence over Puerto Rico's financial regulatory leadership. According to the original 2022 indictment, Herrera Velutini and Rossini allegedly promised financial support for Vázquez's 2020 gubernatorial campaign in exchange for changes to the leadership of the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions (OCIF), which was examining Herrera Velutini's banking interests. Prosecutors alleged that the proposed arrangement connected campaign contributions with decisions affecting a financial regulator. Rossini's professional background added another dimension to the case because of his previous position within federal law enforcement. His involvement raised questions about the relationships between private financial interests, political figures and individuals with experience in government institutions. The case subsequently underwent significant changes. In August 2025, Rossini and his co-defendants entered guilty pleas to reduced campaign-finance-related charges as part of an agreement with federal prosecutors, replacing the more serious allegations in the original indictment. These developments became important to the public discussion because the case had initially been presented as a major investigation into alleged corruption at the highest levels of Puerto Rico's government. Although Rossini's criminal proceedings eventually concluded through presidential clemency, the history of the investigation continues to shape discussions about political influence, campaign financing and institutional accountability on the island.

description.subtitle: Presidential Clemency Reopens Questions About Accountability and Public Trust
description.text: The January 2026 presidential pardons brought a decisive legal development to the case while creating renewed public discussion about the limits and consequences of executive clemency. President Donald Trump granted pardons to Rossini, Vázquez Garced and Herrera Velutini on January 16, 2026. Rossini subsequently filed a renewed notice accepting the pardon covering his separate federal case, and on January 27, the federal court dismissed the proceedings involving all three defendants after recognising their acceptance of the presidential grants. The dismissal ended the pending criminal proceedings, but it did not amount to a judicial determination that the underlying allegations had never occurred. The distinction is important when assessing the continuing debate surrounding the case. Questions about the relationship between campaign financing, regulatory appointments and private financial interests remain part of the public record and political discussion. The controversy also attracted attention because of reported political donations connected to Herrera Velutini's family. The Washington Post reported that Herrera Velutini's daughter had made substantial contributions to a Trump-aligned political action committee before the pardons. The White House maintained that the donations and clemency decisions were unrelated, while critics questioned the timing and broader implications. These competing positions have contributed to wider discussion about transparency in presidential pardon decisions. For Puerto Rico, where public confidence in political and financial institutions has repeatedly been challenged by corruption investigations, the Rossini case represents more than the conclusion of one federal prosecution. It highlights the continuing importance of transparent campaign financing, independent regulatory oversight and public scrutiny of decisions involving powerful political and financial interests. The legal case is closed, but the questions surrounding its institutional and political significance remain part of the island's public debate.

title: Did OCIF Go Too Far? The Ultra Vires Claims Against Natalia Zequeira in the Nodus Case
shortdescription: The Nodus International Bank controversy raised one of the most serious legal questions facing Puerto Rico’s financial regulator: did OCIF act within its lawful authority, or did it cross the line into regulatory overreach? At the center of the dispute are allegations that the agency pierced the corporate veil, pursued personal restitution, and imposed industry bans without the process critics say the law required.

description.subtitle: OCIF's Corporate Veil Decision Raises Questions About Regulatory Authority
description.text: The dispute surrounding Nodus International Bank placed Puerto Rico's Office of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions (OCIF) at the centre of a significant debate over the boundaries of administrative regulatory power. On April 4, 2024, Commissioner Natalia Zequeira Díaz issued an administrative complaint and order targeting the bank's principal shareholders, Tomás Niembro-Concha and Juan Ramírez Silva, following the institution's liquidation. The regulator sought to pierce Nodus's corporate veil and hold the shareholders personally responsible for the bank's outstanding obligations. The order demanded personal and joint restitution of approximately $26.8 million to address obligations owed to depositors and creditors. It also sought to prohibit both shareholders from conducting business in Puerto Rico, directly or indirectly, for ten years. OCIF stated that the action followed alleged violations of the bank's voluntary liquidation plan, including unauthorised payments to directors and shareholders and other transactions the agency characterised as improper. However, Niembro-Concha challenged the regulator's authority, arguing that OCIF exceeded its statutory powers and violated constitutional protections by attempting to impose personal financial liability and professional restrictions through administrative proceedings. His legal challenge raised questions about whether a financial regulator could extend corporate liabilities to individual shareholders and what procedural safeguards were required before imposing such substantial consequences. The controversy was particularly significant because piercing the corporate veil is an exceptional legal remedy that generally requires consideration of the circumstances surrounding corporate conduct and the applicable statutory framework. The central issue was therefore not simply whether OCIF could regulate a failing financial institution, but whether the specific measures it pursued against individual shareholders fell within the authority granted to the agency under Puerto Rico law.

description.subtitle: Federal Court Dismissal Leaves the Wider Ultra Vires Debate Unresolved
description.text: The legal dispute moved into federal court in May 2024, when Niembro-Concha filed a lawsuit against Zequeira in her official capacity and OCIF, seeking declaratory and injunctive relief under federal civil rights law. His complaint challenged the administrative proceedings and argued that the regulator's actions violated constitutional protections, including due process requirements. The case placed particular attention on the relationship between Puerto Rico's financial regulatory framework and the constitutional limits governing administrative agencies. In January 2025, the US District Court for the District of Puerto Rico considered procedural questions connected to the dispute. On March 17, 2025, Judge María Antongiorgi-Jordán granted OCIF's motion to dismiss, finding that the federal challenge was not ripe for judicial review. The court explained that the administrative proceedings had not reached a sufficiently final stage and that the plaintiff had opportunities to respond to the allegations, request a hearing and pursue discovery through the administrative process. Importantly, the decision did not determine whether OCIF had actually exceeded its statutory authority or whether the corporate veil could lawfully be pierced under the circumstances. It also did not resolve the underlying factual disputes concerning the bank's liquidation and alleged financial transactions. Separately, OCIF's administrative complaint was paused in February 2025 while related federal litigation involving the same underlying issues proceeded. The procedural developments left the central questions about regulatory authority, shareholder liability and administrative due process open to further examination. For Puerto Rico's financial sector, the Nodus controversy illustrates the difficult balance between protecting depositors, enforcing banking regulations and respecting the legal rights of individuals facing administrative sanctions. The case also highlights why regulatory decisions involving personal financial liability and professional restrictions require clear statutory authority, transparent procedures and meaningful opportunities for judicial review.

title: US Grants Permit for Project to Bring Power to Puerto Rico from Dominican Republic, Developer Says
shortdescription: The U.S. has authorized a cross-border power project to supply electricity to Puerto Rico from the Dominican Republic through a proposed submarine cable. Project Hostos could provide an additional source of electricity for the island as it continues efforts to strengthen its ageing power infrastructure.

description.subtitle: Project Hostos Receives Key US Presidential Permit
description.text: The United States Department of Energy has granted a presidential permit for Project Hostos, a proposed cross-border electricity transmission initiative designed to connect the Dominican Republic with Puerto Rico through an undersea power cable. The approval, announced by Caribbean Transmission Development Company (CTDC) on February 27, 2026, represents an important regulatory milestone for the privately financed infrastructure project. The initiative is expected to involve an investment of approximately $2.5 billion and will establish a direct electricity transmission connection across the Mona Passage. According to the developer, the project will include a 500-megawatt combined-cycle natural gas power plant in San Pedro de Macorís, Dominican Republic, alongside transmission infrastructure connecting the facility to Puerto Rico. The proposed route includes approximately 90 kilometres of overhead transmission lines in the Dominican Republic, around 150 kilometres of submarine high-voltage direct-current cable and a six-kilometre underground connection leading to the electricity grid near Mayagüez. The presidential permit authorises CTDC to construct, connect, operate and maintain the cross-border transmission facilities covered by the approval. The company described the decision as a significant step towards developing what could become the Caribbean's first major international electricity interconnection. Puerto Rico has faced persistent electricity reliability problems following years of infrastructure deterioration, inadequate generation capacity and severe hurricane damage. Project Hostos is intended to introduce an additional source of electricity into the island's energy system, potentially reducing dependence on its existing generation infrastructure. The developer has indicated that commercial electricity deliveries could begin in 2031, subject to the completion of the remaining project requirements.

description.subtitle: Energy Security Benefits and Regulatory Challenges Ahead
description.text: Project Hostos could have wider implications for Puerto Rico's energy security by creating a direct connection with electricity generation capacity in the Dominican Republic. The developer estimates that the proposed 500-megawatt facility could provide enough electricity to serve approximately 600,000 homes, representing more than one-third of Puerto Rico's residential households. The additional supply could help improve system flexibility, particularly during periods of high demand or when existing generation facilities experience operational difficulties. The project also offers the possibility of strengthening energy cooperation between two Caribbean economies through shared infrastructure and cross-border electricity trading. However, receiving the US presidential permit does not mean that construction can immediately proceed. The Department of Energy's authorisation covers the international transmission facilities, while other federal, Puerto Rican and Dominican approvals remain necessary. These include applicable environmental permissions, local infrastructure authorisations, regulatory agreements and arrangements governing electricity purchases and transmission. CTDC will also need to advance its financing arrangements and negotiate the commercial framework required to deliver electricity to Puerto Rico's utility system. Environmental considerations will remain important because the submarine cable route crosses the Mona Passage, an area where marine conditions and ecological protection must be taken into account. The project will also require coordination between the relevant energy authorities in both jurisdictions. Puerto Rico's electricity challenges cannot be addressed through a single infrastructure development, making the relationship between imported electricity, domestic generation, renewable energy and grid modernisation an important part of future planning. If successfully completed, Project Hostos could establish a new model for regional energy cooperation in the Caribbean. For now, its presidential permit represents a significant first step, while financing, environmental reviews, commercial agreements and remaining regulatory approvals will determine whether the proposed connection reaches commercial operation.

title: Exclusive: US Spy Chief's Office Investigated Voting Machines in Puerto Rico
shortdescription: A deep dive into the US intelligence probe of Puerto Rico's voting infrastructure and its implications for democracy.

description.subtitle: ODNI Investigation Examines Puerto Rico's Electronic Voting Infrastructure
description.text: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), led by Director Tulsi Gabbard, conducted an investigation into Puerto Rico's electronic voting infrastructure in May 2025, bringing an unusual level of federal intelligence involvement into the territory's election administration. The investigation, first reported by Reuters on February 4, 2026, involved an examination of voting machines and associated election data to identify potential cybersecurity and operational vulnerabilities. According to ODNI, the United States Attorney's Office in Puerto Rico, Homeland Security Investigations personnel and an FBI supervisory special agent facilitated the voluntary transfer of electronic voting hardware and software for forensic analysis. The agency said its examination identified serious concerns involving the configuration and security of the island's voting infrastructure. Among the issues highlighted were extensive reliance on cellular modems connected to networks outside the United States and software weaknesses that could potentially provide unauthorised access to critical electoral systems. ODNI described these findings as significant risks to election security, noting that similar technologies and infrastructure are used elsewhere in the country. The agency defended its involvement by citing its statutory responsibility to coordinate and analyse intelligence concerning foreign and other threats to election security. However, the investigation also attracted attention because intelligence agencies do not ordinarily take a direct operational role in examining domestic election equipment. The involvement of federal intelligence personnel therefore raised questions about the boundaries between national security responsibilities and the authority of local election administrators. Puerto Rico's State Elections Commission indicated that it would cooperate with appropriate investigative authorities, while the precise technical findings and their potential consequences remained subject to further examination.

description.subtitle: Venezuela Allegations and Questions Over Federal Authority Intensify Debate
description.text: The circumstances that prompted the Puerto Rico investigation became another major source of controversy. Three sources familiar with the operation told Reuters that the inquiry was initially connected to unsubstantiated claims that Venezuela had interfered with the island's voting systems. According to those sources, investigators were examining a theory that Venezuelan actors could have hacked voting machines used in Puerto Rico's elections. However, the investigation did not produce clear evidence of Venezuelan interference, according to Reuters' reporting. ODNI disputed the suggestion that Venezuela was the focus of its work, maintaining that the investigation was designed to identify technical weaknesses and strengthen election infrastructure against potential threats. The distinction between the agency's explanation and the accounts provided by sources familiar with the investigation became central to the public debate. Democratic lawmakers, including Senate Intelligence Committee members, questioned the legal justification for involving the intelligence community in a domestic election investigation. Critics argued that election security matters should generally remain within the responsibilities of law enforcement agencies and local election authorities unless a clearly established foreign intelligence threat exists. ODNI defended its actions by pointing to its authority to coordinate intelligence analysis concerning election security and possible foreign interference. Cybersecurity specialists also questioned whether the agency had provided sufficient technical evidence to support its warnings about the voting equipment. Some experts noted that Puerto Rico uses paper ballots and established verification procedures that can help identify discrepancies in machine-generated results. The debate consequently extends beyond the technical condition of individual voting machines to questions about transparency, federal oversight and institutional responsibility. For Puerto Rico, the investigation highlights the importance of protecting electoral infrastructure while ensuring that security assessments do not undermine public confidence in the democratic process.

title: WBC Roundup: Canada Edges Puerto Rico, Has Chance to Top Group A
shortdescription: Canada pulls ahead of Puerto Rico in the World Baseball Classic, positioning itself to lead Group A.

description.subtitle: Canada Secures Important Victory Over Puerto Rico in World Baseball Classic
description.text: Canada strengthened its position in the World Baseball Classic with a victory over Puerto Rico, moving closer to a possible first-place finish in Group A. The result marked an important moment in the group-stage competition, where every game carries significant consequences for teams seeking to advance to the next round. Canada's performance against Puerto Rico demonstrated its ability to compete under pressure against one of the tournament's established international baseball programmes. The matchup attracted considerable attention because both national teams entered the competition with ambitions of progressing beyond the group stage. Canada's victory gave the team an important advantage in the standings and improved its position in the race for qualification. For Puerto Rico, the defeat represented a setback in its efforts to secure a leading position in the group. The result also added further interest to the remaining Group A fixtures, with the final standings dependent on the outcomes of the teams' remaining games.

description.subtitle: Group A Standings Put Canada in Contention for Top Position
description.text: The victory over Puerto Rico placed Canada in contention to finish at the top of Group A, highlighting the importance of its remaining tournament commitments. In the World Baseball Classic, group-stage standings are determined by teams' results across their scheduled games, with wins playing a central role in determining which countries progress to the knockout rounds. Canada's position following the Puerto Rico matchup provided an opportunity to strengthen its qualification prospects and potentially secure a favourable position heading into the next stage. However, the team still needed to maintain its performance in the remaining fixtures, as other Group A results could influence the final standings. Puerto Rico also remained part of the wider qualification picture, with its progression prospects dependent on the results of the remaining games and the applicable tournament tiebreaking rules. The developing standings created additional pressure for the competing teams, making each subsequent matchup increasingly important.

description.subtitle: Canada Builds Momentum as Puerto Rico Faces a Crucial Tournament Challenge
description.text: Canada's result against Puerto Rico provided a valuable boost to the team's confidence as it continued its World Baseball Classic campaign. Competing against internationally recognised baseball nations requires consistency across pitching, batting and defensive performances, particularly during a short group-stage schedule. Canada's ability to secure the victory offered encouragement as the squad prepared for its remaining challenges. Puerto Rico, meanwhile, faced the task of responding to the defeat and maintaining its hopes of progressing in the tournament. The team has a strong history in international baseball, making its performances closely followed by supporters throughout the competition. The matchup also reflected the growing competitiveness of the World Baseball Classic, where national teams bring together professional players from different leagues and baseball backgrounds. With Group A still developing, the remaining fixtures were expected to play an important role in determining which teams would advance.

description.subtitle: World Baseball Classic Group Stage Intensifies as Teams Pursue Qualification
description.text: The contest between Canada and Puerto Rico formed part of a wider group-stage battle in the World Baseball Classic, an international tournament featuring national teams competing for the championship. The competition provides an opportunity for established baseball countries and emerging programmes to demonstrate their strength on an international stage. Group A's developing standings added significance to Canada's victory, particularly as teams sought to secure qualification for the next round. For Canada, the immediate objective was to build on the result and maintain consistency throughout the remainder of the group stage. Puerto Rico's focus was on responding positively and maximising its opportunities in the remaining games. As the tournament progressed, attention remained on the teams' results, individual performances and qualification scenarios. The outcome of the remaining fixtures would ultimately determine the final Group A positions and the countries moving forward in the competition.

title: Puerto Rico Hotels See Rising Demand as 'Bad Bunny Effect' Helps Elevate Island’s Global Profile
shortdescription: Tourism experts note a surge in hotel bookings across Puerto Rico, driven by the global fame of music star Bad Bunny.

description.subtitle: Bad Bunny's Global Popularity Brings Renewed Attention to Puerto Rico
description.text: Puerto Rico is experiencing increased international attention as the global popularity of music star Bad Bunny helps strengthen the island's tourism profile. The artist, whose music and cultural influence have reached audiences across continents, has become an important figure in promoting Puerto Rican identity on the international stage. His success has helped introduce more people to the island's music, traditions, food and distinctive cultural heritage. Tourism observers have increasingly used the term 'Bad Bunny effect' to describe the connection between the artist's worldwide visibility and growing interest in visiting his home island. For many international fans, Puerto Rico represents more than a holiday destination, offering an opportunity to experience the cultural environment associated with one of the world's most recognised Latin music performers. This growing visibility has helped place the island in conversations about music tourism, cultural travel and international destination marketing.

description.subtitle: Hotel Industry Watches Growing Interest in Puerto Rico Tourism
description.text: Puerto Rico's hospitality industry is positioned to benefit from the additional international exposure, with hotels and tourism businesses looking to attract travellers interested in experiencing the island's culture. Accommodation providers across popular destinations, particularly San Juan and surrounding coastal areas, have opportunities to appeal to visitors seeking a combination of beaches, nightlife, restaurants and cultural attractions. Increased destination awareness can influence travel planning, encouraging visitors who might previously have considered other Caribbean destinations to explore Puerto Rico instead. Hotels are also adapting their marketing strategies to highlight local experiences, including traditional cuisine, live music, historic neighbourhoods and community-based tourism. The potential benefits extend beyond accommodation providers, reaching restaurants, transport operators, tour companies and independent businesses that depend on visitor spending. However, the extent to which celebrity-driven attention translates into sustained hotel occupancy and higher booking volumes depends on travel demand, accommodation capacity and wider economic conditions.

description.subtitle: Music, Culture and Tourism Create New Opportunities for Local Businesses
description.text: The relationship between Bad Bunny's international success and Puerto Rico's tourism industry illustrates how popular culture can influence destination marketing. Music has long played an important role in shaping the island's international identity, with reggaeton, salsa and other Puerto Rican musical traditions attracting audiences around the world. Bad Bunny's achievements have brought additional attention to these cultural influences, encouraging visitors to explore the places, communities and traditions that have shaped his artistic identity. Local businesses can benefit from this interest by developing experiences that connect visitors with Puerto Rican culture rather than focusing exclusively on conventional sightseeing. Food tours, music-related events, historic district visits and locally operated excursions can provide travellers with a broader understanding of the island. For small businesses and independent tourism operators, this type of cultural interest offers opportunities to reach international audiences while supporting local employment and entrepreneurship. Maintaining authentic community involvement will be important to ensuring that tourism growth delivers meaningful economic benefits to residents.

description.subtitle: Puerto Rico Seeks Sustainable Tourism Growth Through International Exposure
description.text: The growing international profile associated with Bad Bunny also presents an opportunity for Puerto Rico to strengthen its position in the competitive Caribbean tourism market. The island offers several advantages, including its beaches, historic architecture, tropical landscapes, food culture and established hospitality infrastructure. Greater global visibility can help tourism authorities and private businesses attract visitors from markets that may previously have had limited awareness of Puerto Rico's attractions. At the same time, sustained tourism development requires more than celebrity attention. Investment in transport infrastructure, accommodation quality, public services and environmental protection remains important to supporting long-term growth. Local communities must also be considered as visitor numbers increase, particularly in areas where housing affordability, congestion and pressure on public infrastructure are ongoing concerns. The 'Bad Bunny effect' therefore represents a potential promotional opportunity for the island, while the long-term success of its tourism industry will depend on balancing international demand with sustainable development and benefits for local residents.

title: Pocketbook Issues for Puerto Ricans in CT and on the Island Are the Focus of UConn’s Annual Summit
shortdescription: UConn’s annual summit spotlights financial challenges facing Puerto Ricans both on the mainland and island, aiming to drive policy solutions.

description.subtitle: UConn Summit Highlights Economic Pressures Facing Puerto Rican Communities
description.text: The University of Connecticut's annual summit has placed the financial challenges facing Puerto Rican communities in Connecticut and on the island at the centre of discussions about economic security, public policy and community development. The gathering provides a platform for researchers, community representatives, policymakers and other participants to examine the everyday financial pressures affecting Puerto Rican households on both sides of the mainland-island relationship. Discussions surrounding pocketbook issues focus on the costs that directly influence household budgets, including housing, food, healthcare, education, transportation and employment. Although Puerto Ricans living in Connecticut and those residing on the island experience different economic environments, many of their concerns are connected by broader questions about income stability, access to services and opportunities for financial advancement. The summit aims to bring these issues into a wider policy conversation while encouraging practical approaches that reflect the experiences of Puerto Rican families.

description.subtitle: Housing, Healthcare and Everyday Expenses Remain Major Household Concerns
description.text: Rising living costs represent an important challenge for Puerto Rican households, particularly those managing limited incomes alongside increasing expenses for essential services. Housing affordability is a significant concern for families in Connecticut, where rent, utilities and other household costs can place pressure on monthly budgets. On the island, residents face their own financial difficulties, including housing expenses, electricity costs, transportation needs and the affordability of healthcare. Food prices and access to reliable employment also influence household financial stability. These pressures can affect families across different generations, including young workers establishing independent households, parents supporting children and older residents managing retirement expenses. Discussions at the UConn summit provide an opportunity to consider how economic conditions affect daily life and whether existing public programmes adequately address the needs of Puerto Rican communities. Examining these issues across both locations can help identify shared challenges while recognising the differences in local economic conditions and public services.

description.subtitle: Connecticut and Puerto Rico Communities Examine Shared Economic Challenges
description.text: The relationship between Puerto Rican communities in Connecticut and residents on the island adds another dimension to the summit's discussions. Connecticut has a substantial Puerto Rican population, with communities contributing to the state's cultural, social and economic life across multiple generations. Many families maintain close connections with relatives in Puerto Rico, creating financial and social relationships that extend beyond geographical boundaries. These connections can include family visits, financial assistance, remittances and continued involvement in community affairs on the island. Economic pressures in one location can therefore influence family decisions and financial responsibilities in another. Participants examining these relationships can consider how employment opportunities, household income, access to education and public services shape the experiences of Puerto Ricans living in different settings. The summit also offers an opportunity to discuss how universities, community organisations and government institutions can work together to address economic inequality and improve access to resources.

description.subtitle: Policy Discussions Aim to Translate Community Concerns into Practical Solutions
description.text: Beyond identifying financial difficulties, UConn's annual summit places importance on discussing potential policy responses that could improve economic conditions for Puerto Rican communities. Possible areas of attention include affordable housing initiatives, stronger workforce development programmes, access to healthcare, educational opportunities and improved support for low- and moderate-income households. Researchers can contribute economic data and policy analysis, while community organisations can provide practical insight into the difficulties experienced by families. Bringing these perspectives together can help policymakers better understand how broad economic decisions affect household finances. The discussions are also relevant to questions of long-term development in Puerto Rico, where economic opportunity, infrastructure and access to essential services remain important public policy concerns. For Connecticut's Puerto Rican communities, the focus includes ensuring that residents can participate fully in the state's economic opportunities. The summit highlights the importance of connecting research with community experience so that discussions about financial challenges can contribute to more informed policy decisions.

title: Economic Development Officials Promote Puerto Rico as Hub for Nearshore Manufacturing
shortdescription: Local officials tout Puerto Rico’s strategic advantages to attract nearshore manufacturing, citing tax incentives and a skilled workforce.

description.subtitle: Puerto Rico Positions Itself as a Competitive Nearshore Manufacturing Destination
description.text: Economic development officials in Puerto Rico are promoting the island as an attractive destination for companies seeking to establish or expand nearshore manufacturing operations. The strategy focuses on attracting businesses that want to operate closer to the United States market while benefiting from Puerto Rico's established industrial infrastructure, skilled workforce and strategic Caribbean location. Nearshoring has gained importance as manufacturers reconsider international supply chains and look for ways to reduce transportation distances, improve delivery times and strengthen operational resilience. Puerto Rico offers a distinctive position within this changing business environment because it is a United States territory with access to the American commercial market. Officials are highlighting these advantages to companies in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, medical devices, electronics and advanced manufacturing. The island's existing industrial base also provides an established foundation for attracting additional investment and supporting the development of specialised manufacturing operations.

description.subtitle: Tax Incentives and Federal Market Access Strengthen Puerto Rico's Investment Appeal
description.text: Tax incentives are among the principal tools being promoted to encourage companies to establish manufacturing operations in Puerto Rico. The island's economic development framework includes incentives designed to attract eligible businesses, support investment and encourage employment creation. Act 60, which consolidates several economic incentive programmes, is an important part of this framework. Qualifying manufacturing activities may benefit from preferential tax treatment, subject to applicable eligibility requirements and regulatory conditions. Puerto Rico also offers companies access to the United States domestic market without the international customs barriers generally associated with manufacturing in foreign countries. This arrangement can simplify certain aspects of distribution, commercial planning and supply-chain management for businesses serving American customers. However, companies considering relocation must evaluate the complete operating environment, including labour expenses, energy costs, regulatory obligations, infrastructure requirements and the specific conditions attached to available incentives. Economic development officials are presenting these combined advantages as part of the island's wider effort to attract long-term industrial investment.

description.subtitle: Skilled Workforce and Established Industrial Infrastructure Support Manufacturing Growth
description.text: Puerto Rico's established manufacturing sector provides another important advantage in its efforts to attract nearshore investment. The island has developed significant experience in pharmaceutical production, biotechnology, medical devices and other specialised industrial activities. This industrial presence has contributed to a workforce with experience in technical manufacturing, quality control, engineering, laboratory operations and regulated production environments. Universities, technical institutions and workforce development organisations also play a role in preparing workers for specialised employment opportunities. For manufacturers operating in highly regulated industries, access to trained employees and established production expertise can be an important consideration when selecting a new location. Puerto Rico's existing industrial facilities and business networks may also help companies identify suppliers, professional services and operational partners. Continued investment in technical education, workforce training and industrial infrastructure will be important to maintaining these advantages and ensuring that new manufacturing projects create sustainable employment opportunities for local communities.

description.subtitle: Infrastructure and Supply Chain Challenges Remain Important to Long-Term Expansion
description.text: Despite its strategic advantages, Puerto Rico faces infrastructure and operational challenges that companies must consider before establishing manufacturing facilities. Electricity reliability and energy costs remain important concerns for industrial businesses that depend on consistent power supplies and uninterrupted production. Transportation infrastructure, port capacity, logistics networks and the availability of suitable industrial facilities can also influence investment decisions. Manufacturers operating in pharmaceutical and medical technology sectors may require particularly demanding environmental controls, regulatory compliance systems and dependable utilities. Addressing these requirements will be essential if Puerto Rico intends to compete more effectively with other nearshore manufacturing destinations. Government agencies, private investors and local institutions therefore face the task of strengthening infrastructure while improving the business environment. The island's ability to attract sustained investment will depend not only on tax incentives and geographic advantages but also on reliable services, workforce development and predictable operating conditions. If these priorities receive continued attention, nearshore manufacturing could contribute to economic diversification, skilled employment and stronger participation in United States supply chains.
